UserPromptSubmit.description: Surface newly-tapped status-board answers into context. The board records answers server-side and notifies nobody; relying on the agent to remember to read the file failed within an hour of the rule being written. Durable but slow: it can only fire when the owner sends a message, so a tap waits for their next prompt. That latency is what SessionStart's arm-watcher removes — keep both, they fail differently.

SessionStart.description: Instruct the agent to arm the answer watcher, so a tap arrives in seconds rather than on the owner's next message. Silent for projects with no board. A hook cannot call the Monitor tool, so this is a reliably-delivered instruction rather than a mechanism — weaker than board-answers.py by design, and the strongest option available for something that requires a tool call.

Offer the bootstrap in a folder with no team structure. A new session in a new folder never suggested /project-bootstrap, so the working practice this plugin exists to provide arrived only if the owner remembered to ask. A hook cannot run a skill, only instruct the agent, so like arm-watcher's this is an instruction — and it insists on the order: ask what the project is and who works on it, get a yes, only then scaffold. Silent when .claude/rules/team-roles.md exists at the cwd or its git top-level (a bare .claude/ proves nothing: Claude Code creates settings.local.json itself), in $HOME, / and ~/.claude, on resume/compact/fork, in an agent session, and when opted out (PROJECT_INIT_NO_OFFER=1, or an empty .claude/no-bootstrap-offer). Fails quiet: any error prints nothing and exits 0, so a bug costs the offer, not the session. A pane teammate is recognised by agent_type/agent_id, or by --agent-id/--parent-session-id on an ancestor process; neither has been seen in a live teammate yet, so one may still see the offer — noise, not damage.

Restart a project's status board that is not running. A board's state survives a reboot but its server does not, and the owner found out by opening a dead URL. If the project has a board and nothing answers on its port (derived by serve.py itself — imported, not copied, so the two cannot disagree), this starts serve.py detached, logging to boards/<slug>/serve.log, and prints the URL. It does nothing if the board page already answers; if something else holds the port it starts nothing and says so in one line. Fails quiet but not blind: it always exits 0 and never waits more than a few seconds, and when it cannot bring the board up it prints one line pointing at the log. Limits: it restarts with serve.py's defaults (loopback only; the folder name as display name, since serve.py stores none), and it cannot tell another project's board on the same derived port from this one.

PreToolUse.description: Deny a dispatch that would grant a second agent the working tree while another already holds it — "one agent owns the working tree at a time" was already written in team-roles.md and verification.md and was broken twice anyway, including once while the lead was actively quoting it. A rule that has been read and re-broken is proof the rule is the wrong instrument; this is the mechanism instead. Silent for a dispatch that is not tree-mutating (repo-inventory, architect, qa), for isolation: "worktree" dispatches, and for a role resuming itself. See status-board/tree_lock.py for the lock state both this hook and the board read.
